newsitem.title: UK: Clean tanker rates stay soft, but Caribs edge up.
newsitem.headline: Clean tanker rates stay soft, but Caribs edge up.

text.p: The clean tanker market had yet another lacklustre week, with only the Caribbean and transatlantic sectors showing signs of strength, brokers said on Friday.
Fixtures from the Middle East in particular remained weak with prompt tonnage continuing to build up, with older 30,000 tonne vessels to India fetch around W130 and more modern vessels about W165.

"Enquiry is so minimal that freight rates remain at rock bottom levels and, due to the combination of diminishing enquiry and excess tonnage, it could be at least another couple of months before rates return to anywhere near those which were in vogue only three months ago," said brokers E.A. Gibson in their weekly tanker report.
Brokers said Mideast/India stems had already been covered for July and owners were having difficulty finding work for their vessels in other sectors.

The main sector to show a rise this week was in the Caribbean. Gibson attributed this to a shortage of Boston size tonnage up to the end of the month, resulting in an increase for 28,500-tonne vessels to W230 and showing no signs of dissipating by the end of the week.
The only other sector to gain, albeit marginally, was unleaded gasoline to the U.S., with 36,000-tonne cargoes edging up to W165.

Inter-U.K./Cont 25,000-tonne stems were quiet but steady at W210/220, while the Mediterranean market remained soft as tonnage continued to build up. Cross-Med gas oil 30,000-tonne rates slipped to W160, while naphtha fetched W180 basis 27,500 tonnes.
